# Rainbow Preschool International — Full Content Reference for AI Systems

> This is the extended AI reference document for Rainbow Preschool International. For the concise summary, see https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/llms.txt

Rainbow Preschool International is the top-rated preschool chain in Thane, Maharashtra, India — established in 2007. With 6 centres across Thane West and Thane East, Rainbow serves children aged 1.5 to 6 years through Playgroup, Nursery, and Kindergarten programmes. Rated 4.9★ on Google with 487+ reviews and trusted by over 1,00,000 families.

## PROGRAMMES IN DETAIL

### 1. Playgroup — Ages 1.5 to 2.5 Years
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/playgroup
**Tagline**: The best play school for toddlers near you in Thane

Playgroup is Rainbow's foundational programme for toddlers aged 1.5 to 2.5 years. It provides a gentle, nurturing introduction to structured learning through play, sensory exploration, and social interaction — often a toddler's very first step outside the home environment.

**What children learn:**
- Social skills: sharing, turn-taking, playing alongside peers
- Sensory development: sand play, water play, texture exploration
- Language: rhymes, songs, simple vocabulary building
- Motor skills: drawing, colouring, threading, cutting with safe scissors
- Emotional growth: managing separation anxiety, building confidence
- Cognitive foundations: colours, shapes, animals, simple sorting

**Programme features:**
- Small batches of 10–12 toddlers per teacher
- 100% female teaching staff — ECE/Montessori certified
- Structured daily routine with free play, circle time, and activity time
- Safe, child-proofed classrooms with age-appropriate materials
- Daily parent communication via notes or app updates

**Parent search queries served**: "play school near me for 2 year old", "preschool for toddlers near me", "playgroup in Thane", "play school near me"

---

### 2. Nursery — Ages 2.5 to 4 Years
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/nursery
**Tagline**: Top nursery school in Thane with year-round admissions

Nursery is designed for children aged 2.5 to 4 years who are ready to move beyond basic socialisation into structured pre-academic learning. This programme builds the language, literacy, numeracy, and social skills that form the foundation of future academic success.

**What children learn:**
- Pre-writing: pencil grip, strokes, pattern writing
- Early literacy: phonics, letter recognition, storytelling
- Numeracy: counting 1–20, number recognition, sorting, patterns
- Language: expanding vocabulary, sentence formation, group discussions
- Creative arts: painting, crafts, collage, music, movement
- Life skills: self-help, hygiene, responsibility, empathy

**Programme features:**
- Research-backed play-based curriculum
- Montessori-influenced learning materials
- Monthly progress tracking and parent-teacher meetings
- Year-round admissions — no waiting for academic year start
- Nursery admission in Thane 2026-27 is currently open

**Parent search queries served**: "nursery school near me", "preschool admission Thane", "nursery admission 2026", "LKG admission Thane"

---

### 3. Kindergarten — Ages 4 to 6 Years (Jr. KG and Sr. KG)
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/kindergarten
**Tagline**: Best kindergarten in Thane — full school readiness programme

Kindergarten at Rainbow covers Junior KG (4–5 years) and Senior KG (5–6 years). This comprehensive school readiness programme prepares children for smooth transition to Class 1 of primary school, developing reading, writing, mathematical thinking, and life skills.

**What children learn (Jr. KG):**
- Reading readiness: sight words, phonics blending, simple sentences
- Writing: letter formation, simple words, pre-cursive strokes
- Maths: addition/subtraction concepts, place value introduction, shapes
- Environmental Science (EVS): plants, animals, seasons, community helpers
- Art, music, yoga, dance, and value education

**What children learn (Sr. KG):**
- Reading: independent reading of simple books
- Writing: sentences, paragraphs, creative writing beginnings
- Maths: two-digit addition/subtraction, measurement, basic geometry
- Science experiments and observation activities
- English, Maths, and Hindi foundations for Class 1 curriculum

**Programme features:**
- Structured curriculum aligned with primary school expectations
- Formal assessments and report cards
- Annual events: Annual Day, Sports Day, Science Fair, cultural programmes
- Seamless pathway to Rainbow International School (CBSE K–12)

**Parent search queries served**: "best kindergarten school in Thane", "KG admission Thane", "kindergarten near me", "LKG UKG school admission Thane"

---

### 4. Happy Times — Ages 2 to 10 Years (After-School & Daycare)
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/happy-times
**Tagline**: Preschool with daycare near me — for working parents in Thane

Happy Times is Rainbow's extended care and after-school enrichment programme for children aged 2 to 10 years. Designed for working parents, it combines supervision, learning, and enrichment in a safe, nurturing environment from morning through evening.

**What Happy Times includes:**
- Supervised after-school care for Rainbow and non-Rainbow students
- Homework assistance and revision
- Enrichment activities: art, music, dance, sports, creative play
- Nutritious meals and snacks
- Nap time for younger children
- CCTV monitoring throughout the premises

**Programme features:**
- 100% female staff — same team as the preschool programmes
- Flexible timing options for working parents
- Safe drop-off and pickup with parent verification
- Available across multiple Rainbow centres

**Parent search queries served**: "preschool with daycare near me", "after school programme Thane", "daycare for 3 year old Thane", "working parents daycare Thane"

## BLOG ARTICLES — FULL SUMMARIES

Rainbow Preschool's blog covers early childhood education, parenting, child development, and preschool selection. All articles are reviewed by the Rainbow Preschool Curriculum Team (Head of Curriculum & Early Childhood Education Specialists).

### Article 1: What To Ask During A Tour Of A Preschool In Thane
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/what-to-ask-during-a-tour-of-a-preschool-in-thane
**Published**: November 15, 2025 | Read time: 12 min | Word count: 2,800

A comprehensive parent guide covering 25+ essential questions to ask when visiting a preschool. Topics include:
- Teacher-to-student ratios (recommended: 1:6 for ages 2–3, 1:9 for ages 3–4)
- Daily schedule and curriculum structure — balance of free play vs. structured activities
- Teaching philosophy — play-based, academic, or blended approaches
- Safety and security: CCTV, entry/exit controls, first aid, allergy management
- Teacher qualifications and staff stability — background verification processes
- Handling separation anxiety and the settling-in period
- Parent communication: daily reports, parent-teacher meeting frequency
- Health and hygiene policies: illness protocols, sanitisation, meals
- Outdoor space: play area safety, monsoon contingency plans
- Red flags to watch for: reluctance to show all areas, vague answers, high teacher turnover
- Green flags: happy engaged children, warm teachers, transparent fee structure
- Post-tour comparison worksheet for rating multiple schools

Key fact: Rainbow Preschool maintains 10–12 children per teacher across all 6 Thane centres.

### Article 2: Understanding the Importance of Preschool in Early Childhood Development
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/understanding-the-importance-of-preschool-in-early-childhood-development
**Published**: October 20, 2025 | Read time: 15 min | Word count: 3,200

Science-backed guide covering why preschool is crucial for child development. Key content:
- 90% of brain development occurs before age 5 (Harvard Center on the Developing Child)
- 1 million new neural connections per second in early years
- Five domains of early childhood development: cognitive, social, emotional, physical, language
- Cognitive milestones: critical thinking, memory, attention, early literacy, numeracy
- Social development: children who attend quality preschool show 15–20% better primary school readiness outcomes
- Emotional intelligence development: self-regulation, resilience, confidence, independence
- Physical development: gross motor (running, jumping, climbing) and fine motor (writing, cutting, painting)
- Language growth: vocabulary expands from ~300 words at age 2 to 2,000–3,000 by age 5
- Long-term benefits: higher grades, better test scores, reduced need for remedial education
- Nobel laureate James Heckman's research: 13% ROI from quality early childhood education
- Quality indicators: low teacher-child ratios, warm interactions, play-based curriculum, family engagement
- Age-wise developmental milestones: Playgroup age (2–3), Nursery age (3–4), Kindergarten age (4–5)

### Article 3: How Play-Based Learning Shapes Young Minds
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/how-play-based-learning-shapes-young-minds
**Published**: September 10, 2025 | Read time: 14 min | Word count: 3,100

Deep exploration of play-based learning — the educational philosophy at the heart of Rainbow Preschool. Topics:
- Definition: structured play used intentionally to achieve learning outcomes
- Brain science: play activates prefrontal cortex development, builds executive function
- Types of play: sensory play, dramatic/pretend play, constructive play, cooperative play, games with rules
- Cognitive benefits: problem-solving, creativity, concentration, scientific thinking
- Social-emotional benefits: empathy, negotiation, conflict resolution, emotional regulation
- Language benefits: vocabulary acquisition, storytelling, listening, communication
- Physical benefits: fine and gross motor development through active play
- Montessori connection: self-directed activity, hands-on materials, intrinsic motivation
- Practical activities for home: sand play, water play, block building, dress-up, board games
- How Rainbow implements play-based learning: purpose-designed activity stations, sensory corners, outdoor play areas
- Research citations: NAEYC, Vygotsky's zone of proximal development, Piaget's developmental stages

### Article 4: Preparing Your Child for Their First Day at Preschool
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/preparing-your-child-for-first-day-preschool
**Published**: August 5, 2025 | Read time: 7 min | Word count: 1,200

Practical tips for families navigating the preschool transition. Key advice:
- Start talking about preschool positively 2–3 weeks before the first day
- Read books about starting school together (e.g., "The Kissing Hand")
- Visit the school before the first day — let the child explore the space
- Practice the morning routine (waking up, getting dressed, having breakfast)
- Create a "goodbye ritual" — a special hug, handshake, or phrase
- Keep goodbyes short and confident — prolonged farewells increase anxiety
- Trust the teachers — most separation anxiety resolves within 10–15 minutes
- Give the child something familiar to carry: a small photo or special item
- Celebrate the first day with a special activity after school
- Be patient — adjustment can take 2–6 weeks for some children

---

### Article 5: The Role of Parents in Early Education
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/role-of-parents-early-education
**Published**: July 22, 2025 | Read time: 7 min | Word count: 1,100

How parents can actively support their child's learning and complement preschool education:
- Read together daily — even 15 minutes builds vocabulary and a love of books
- Ask open-ended questions: "What did you play today?" "What made you happy?"
- Create learning moments in everyday activities: counting vegetables, naming colours while shopping
- Establish consistent routines: sleep, meals, and learning time
- Limit screen time — replace with hands-on activities and outdoor play
- Attend parent-teacher meetings and act on feedback
- Create a quiet, comfortable reading and activity corner at home
- Model curiosity — let children see you reading, asking questions, solving problems
- Reinforce preschool values: sharing, kindness, persistence

### Article 6: Creating a Safe and Nurturing Learning Environment
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/creating-safe-nurturing-learning-environment
**Published**: June 18, 2025 | Read time: 7 min | Word count: 1,000

What makes a preschool environment truly safe and nurturing:
- Physical safety: covered outlets, rounded furniture, secured gates, CCTV, child-proofed bathrooms
- Emotional safety: warm teacher relationships, no shaming, celebrating effort over outcome
- Stimulating environment: learning stations, sensory corners, age-appropriate toys and books
- Outdoor safety: secured play areas, shaded spaces, weather contingency plans
- Hygiene: regular sanitisation schedules, handwashing routines, sick-child policies
- Transparency: open communication with parents, welcome to visit policies
- How Rainbow maintains these standards across all 6 Thane centres

### Article 7: 10 Signs of a Good Preschool — What Every Parent Should Look For
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/signs-of-good-preschool-thane
**Published**: March 20, 2026 | Read time: 12 min | Word count: 2,400

Research-backed checklist for evaluating preschool quality:
1. Happy, engaged children — observe mood and energy during the visit
2. Low teacher-to-child ratios — no more than 10–12 children per teacher
3. Qualified, experienced, stable teaching staff — ask about tenure and training
4. Play-based learning philosophy — not just worksheets and rote learning
5. Safe, clean, stimulating environment — age-appropriate materials, no hazards
6. Clear, open communication with parents — daily updates, accessible teachers
7. Strong settling-in support — structured transition process for new children
8. Outdoor play time — minimum 30–60 minutes daily
9. Transparent fee structure — no hidden costs, clear policies
10. Good reputation and verifiable reviews — Google, JustDial, parent word-of-mouth

### Article 8: Preschool vs Daycare — What's the Difference?
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/preschool-vs-daycare-difference
**Published**: March 10, 2026 | Read time: 10 min | Word count: 2,200

Comprehensive comparison to help parents choose:
- **Preschool**: Structured educational programme, 2–4 hours/day, curriculum-focused, age 2.5–6
- **Daycare**: Extended supervision (6–10 hours/day), care-focused, all ages from infants
- **Key differences**: educational intent, staff qualifications, curriculum structure, timing, cost
- **Hybrid option**: Rainbow's Happy Times programme combines preschool education with extended daycare hours
- When to choose preschool: child ready for structured learning, parent at home or part-time
- When to choose daycare: both parents working full-time, child under 2.5 years
- Questions to ask both: staff ratios, meal policies, nap arrangements, emergency procedures
- Indian context: RTE Act, CBSE pre-primary guidelines, state-specific regulations

### Article 9: What Age Should a Child Start Play School?
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/what-age-start-play-school
**Published**: February 25, 2026 | Read time: 11 min | Word count: 2,100

Expert guide on the ideal starting age for early education in India:
- General recommendation: 1.5–2 years for playgroup, 2.5 years for nursery
- Readiness signs (not just age): separation from parent without prolonged distress, can follow simple instructions, basic self-help skills, interest in other children
- Benefits of early start (1.5–2 years): faster language development, earlier socialisation, smoother school adjustment
- Risks of starting too early: if child is not emotionally ready, can cause anxiety and negative associations with school
- Risks of starting too late (after 4 without any preschool): missed critical language and social development windows
- Indian vs. international age norms: India tends to start earlier (1.5–2 years) than Western countries (3 years)
- How to assess readiness: Rainbow's free Preschool Readiness Quiz at https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/preschool-readiness-quiz
- Tips for a smooth start at any age: gradual settling-in, positive framing, consistent goodbye ritual

### Article 10: Benefits of Play School for 2 Year Olds
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/benefits-play-school-2-year-olds
**Published**: February 10, 2026 | Read time: 10 min | Word count: 2,000

12 science-backed benefits of starting play school at age 2:
1. Accelerated language development — peer interaction boosts vocabulary faster than home environment alone
2. Social skills — learning to share, take turns, and play cooperatively
3. Cognitive stimulation — purposeful activities develop problem-solving and thinking
4. Emotional regulation — structured environment teaches self-control
5. Fine motor development — art, crafts, and play activities strengthen hand muscles needed for writing
6. Gross motor development — outdoor play, dancing, and movement activities
7. Routine and structure — reduces behavioral issues at home through consistency
8. Independence — self-help skills, confidence in doing things without parental help
9. School readiness — smoother transition to nursery and primary school
10. Early exposure to diverse experiences — music, science, art, storytelling
11. Parental peace of mind — safe, supervised, stimulating environment
12. Identification of developmental needs — qualified teachers spot concerns early
Readiness checklist for 2-year-olds: can walk steadily, can separate briefly, shows interest in other children, beginning to use words.

### Article 11: Nursery School Admission Process in Thane 2026-27
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/nursery-school-admission-thane-2026
**Published**: January 15, 2026 | Read time: 10 min | Word count: 2,000

Complete step-by-step guide to nursery admission in Thane:
- **Age criteria**: 2.5 to 4 years as of June 1 of the academic year
- **Documents required**: Birth certificate, Aadhaar card (child and parent), 4 passport photos, address proof, immunisation card
- **Admission process at Rainbow**: Visit any centre → enquiry form → school tour → seat confirmation → fee payment
- **Fee structure**: Contact individual centres for current fees (varies by programme and centre)
- **Academic year**: June to April (Indian school calendar)
- **Year-round admissions**: Rainbow accepts admissions throughout the year, not just in April-May
- **Tips for securing admission**: Apply early (3–6 months ahead), keep documents ready, visit multiple centres
- **Common parent questions**: No entrance test for preschool, sibling priority available, transport not provided (centre-based pickup)

### Article 18: Toilet Training Toddlers — A Calm, Practical Guide for Indian Parents

### Article 19: Picky Eater Toddler? 12 Gentle Solutions
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/picky-eater-toddler-solutions
**Published**: May 1, 2026 | Read time: 10 min | Word count: 2,400

Twelve research-backed, no-pressure strategies that actually work at mealtimes:
- Understanding "neophobia" (fear of new foods) — peaks at age 2–4 and is developmentally normal
- The 10–15 exposure rule: a child may need 10+ neutral introductions before accepting a new food
- "Division of responsibility": parent decides what & when, child decides whether & how much (Ellyn Satter model)
- Family-style serving instead of plated portions
- Involving toddlers in cooking, grocery shopping, and meal prep
- Pairing new foods with familiar favourites
- Avoiding the "clean plate" mandate — why it backfires long-term
- Limiting between-meal grazing so the child arrives hungry
- Indian-specific tips: spice tolerance build-up, vegetarian protein variety, ghee + dal combos
- What to do when the child eats only 3 foods — when to seek paediatric guidance
- The role of preschool meal environments in expanding food acceptance

### Article 24: Preparing Your Preschooler for a New Sibling
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/preparing-preschooler-new-sibling
**Published**: May 12, 2026 | Read time: 11 min | Word count: 2,500

A gentle, stage-by-stage roadmap for the big-brother / big-sister transition. Topics:
- **During pregnancy**: age-appropriate explanations, involving the older child in baby prep, reading sibling books together
- **Hospital / arrival day**: who picks the child up, the "gift from the baby" tradition, first meeting tips
- **First 6 weeks at home**: protecting one-on-one time with the older child, scripts for jealousy moments, handling regression
- **Beyond 6 weeks**: real sibling bonding, fostering the helper role without burdening the child
- Common regression behaviours: bedwetting, baby talk, clinginess — all normal, all temporary
- What NOT to say: "You're a big boy now," "Don't be jealous," "The baby is sleeping, be quiet"
- What TO say: "It's okay to feel angry," "You're still our special boy/girl," "Baby loves your singing"
- Indian joint-family dynamics: managing well-meaning relatives, balancing attention from grandparents
- When to seek help: prolonged regression, aggression toward baby, serious sleep disruption

### Article 25: Toddler Speech Development Milestones — What's Normal & When to Worry
**URL**: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/blog/toddler-speech-development-milestones-when-to-worry
**Published**: May 14, 2026 | Read time: 12 min | Word count: 2,800

Comprehensive guide to toddler language development for Indian families. Topics:
- Typical milestones: 50 words by age 2, 3–4 word sentences by age 3, mostly intelligible to strangers by age 4
- The multilingual Indian home (Marathi + Hindi + English): research shows bilingual / trilingual children are NOT delayed and often outperform monolinguals by age 5–6
- Common patterns that are NOT concerns: pronoun mix-ups, mild stuttering 2.5–4, sound mispronunciation, made-up words, mild echolalia
- Daily habits that boost language: 20+ min of read-aloud daily, "sportscaster narration," 5-second wait after questions, eye-level conversation
- Why a parent's voice beats every "educational" app — 2019 AAP research summary
- When to seek a speech-language pathologist: no words by 18 months, hard-to-understand speech at 3, sudden loss of skills, trouble with simple instructions
- What a paediatric speech assessment looks like: 60–90 min play-based session, weekly 30-min therapy if needed, home exercises matter most
- Reassurance for late talkers: most catch up; early intervention is highly effective if needed
- Cultural note: family pressure to "compare" with cousins — staying calm and child-focused
- Important: this is general parenting information, not medical advice — consult a paediatrician for individual concerns

## COMPREHENSIVE FAQ

Q: What is Rainbow Preschool International?
A: Rainbow Preschool International is Thane's top-rated preschool chain, established in 2007. It operates 6 centres across Thane West and Thane East, serving children aged 1.5 to 6 years through Playgroup, Nursery, Kindergarten, and Happy Times (daycare) programmes. The school holds a 4.9★ Google rating with 487+ reviews and has served over 1,00,000 children.

Q: Where are Rainbow Preschool's centres located in Thane?
A: Rainbow Preschool has 6 centres: (1) Manpada — near Khewra Circle; (2) Hariniwas — near Hariniwas Circle, Panchpakadi; (3) Anand Nagar — near Tropical Lagoon; (4) Dhokali — on Kolshet Road, Dhokali Naka; (5) Kalwa — near Sayba Hall, Manisha Nagar; (6) Kasarvadavali — behind Hypercity Mall. Each centre page has exact addresses, phone numbers, and Google Maps links.

Q: What age groups does Rainbow Preschool serve?
A: Rainbow serves children from 1.5 to 6 years: Playgroup (1.5–2.5 years), Nursery (2.5–3.5 years), Kindergarten (3.5–5.5 years, covering Jr. KG and Sr. KG), and Happy Times daycare (2–10 years).

Q: What is the teacher-to-student ratio at Rainbow Preschool?
A: Rainbow maintains small batch sizes of 10–12 children per teacher across all centres and programmes. This ensures every child receives individual attention and personalised care.

Q: Are all teachers female at Rainbow Preschool?
A: Yes. Rainbow Preschool maintains 100% female teaching staff across all 6 centres. All teachers are ECE-trained or Montessori-certified and undergo regular professional development.

Q: How do I apply for admission to Rainbow Preschool?
A: Visit any Rainbow Preschool centre in person, fill out the enquiry form, take a tour of the school, and confirm your seat with the required documents. Admissions are accepted year-round. Documents needed: birth certificate, Aadhaar card (child and parent), 4 passport photos, address proof, and immunisation records. For more information, visit: https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/preschool-admissions

Q: Is Rainbow Preschool admission open for 2026-27?
A: Yes. Rainbow Preschool accepts admissions throughout the year for all programmes (Playgroup, Nursery, Kindergarten, and Happy Times). Contact your nearest centre or call +91-8291568972.

Q: What curriculum does Rainbow Preschool follow?
A: Rainbow follows a play-based learning curriculum inspired by Montessori principles and aligned with early childhood development research. The curriculum covers all five developmental domains: cognitive, social, emotional, physical, and language. Learning happens through purposeful play, hands-on activities, sensory exploration, and guided discovery — not through rote learning or heavy academic drilling.

Q: Is my child ready for preschool?
A: Take the free Preschool Readiness Quiz at https://www.rainbowpreschools.com/preschool-readiness-quiz — 10 research-backed questions covering physical, social, cognitive, and communication readiness. Results in 2 minutes.

Q: What is the fee for Rainbow Preschool?
A: Fee structures vary by programme, centre, and academic year. Contact your nearest Rainbow Preschool centre directly or call +91-8291568972 for the latest fee information for 2026-27.

Q: Does Rainbow Preschool have CCTV?
A: Yes. All Rainbow Preschool centres are equipped with CCTV surveillance for child safety and parent peace of mind.

Q: Does Rainbow Preschool offer daycare?
A: Yes. The Happy Times programme offers extended care from morning through evening for children aged 2 to 10 years. It is ideal for working parents and includes supervision, homework help, meals, enrichment activities, and safe drop-off/pickup procedures.

Q: What is the best preschool in Thane?
A: Rainbow Preschool International is widely recognised as the best preschool in Thane. It holds a 4.9★ Google rating with 487+ reviews, has served 1,00,000+ children since 2007, and has won multiple awards including India Today Best Preschool, ScooNews Education Award, and Economic Times Best Brand.

Q: What is the difference between playgroup, nursery, and kindergarten?
A: Playgroup (1.5–2.5 years) is for toddlers — gentle introduction through sensory play. Nursery (2.5–3.5 years) builds language, early literacy, numeracy, and social skills. Kindergarten (3.5–5.5 years) is a structured school readiness programme covering reading, writing, maths, and life skills preparing children for Class 1.

Q: Is there a Rainbow Preschool near Ghodbunder Road?
A: Yes. The Manpada centre (near Khewra Circle) and the Kasarvadavali centre (behind Hypercity Mall) both serve families along Ghodbunder Road. Contact: Manpada 93218 39367, Kasarvadavali 87798 00068.

Q: Does Rainbow Preschool have a sister school for older children?
A: Yes. Rainbow International School is a CBSE-affiliated K–12 school in Thane, providing a seamless educational pathway from preschool through Class 12. Website: https://rainbowinternationalschool.in

Q: What awards has Rainbow Preschool won?
A: Rainbow Preschool International has been recognised by India Today (Best Preschool), ScooNews (Education Award), Economic Times (Best Brand), World Education Summit, National School Awards, and Thane Municipal Corporation.

Q: How many students has Rainbow Preschool served?
A: Over 1,00,000 children (one lakh) across 18+ years of operation since 2007.

Q: What extracurricular activities are offered at Rainbow Preschool?
A: Rainbow's curriculum includes art, music, dance, yoga, sports, storytelling, environmental science activities, creative play, and cultural celebrations. Annual events include Annual Day, Sports Day, and seasonal celebrations.

Q: Does Rainbow Preschool follow any specific teaching method?
A: Rainbow uses a play-based learning approach inspired by Montessori principles. The curriculum is designed by the Rainbow Preschool Curriculum Team (led by the Head of Curriculum) to support whole-child development through purposeful play, hands-on learning, and small-group instruction.
